From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-01 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: BrightData MAP — perf run plan and quick notes

Team — running the benchmarks now. Notes/assumptions for reproducibility:

- Client: our internal harness hitting the Hosted API endpoint (region: us-west-2). Requests use standard SDK with keep-alive.
- Payload distributions: we sampled BrightData docs and built prompt-size buckets: small (<=256 tokens) 45%, medium (257-8k) 30%, long (8k-64k) 20%, ultra-long (>64k) 5%. We'll run synthetic uniform long-window tests for worst-case.
- KV cache: we simulate three modes: 1) Cold: every request new; 2) Warm: repeated prefix cached for 1000s depending on bucket; 3) Sticky: KV retention across chained calls to test sequence growth.
- Measurement: TTFT measured at token 1 emit from server side + client socket handshake; end-to-end adds client network. We'll report median/95th/99th.
- Concurrency: run steady-state for 5 minutes per config, then ramp.

I'll attach raw CSV and a small set of plots. Preliminary observations (quick):
- 8k window (rw-13B on A100): TTFT ~ 38ms median, sustained throughput ~ 1,800 tok/s at concurrency=8, 95th token latency ~ 120ms.
- 64k window (rw-34B on A100, but H100 preferred): TTFT ~ 110ms median (A100), sustained throughput drops ~ 3x vs 8k due to KV and attention compute.
- 256k window on H100: TTFT ~ 380ms median, throughput ~ 420 tok/s at concurrency=8; warm KV improves TTFT by ~18% and throughput by ~25% in our runs.
- 512k window on H100: memory-limited for 34B; we had to run quantized variants and saw TTFT ~ 900ms median, throughput ~ 180 tok/s at concurrency=1; concurrency=8 caused queuing and TTFT tail spikes.

I'll push the CSV + plots to Drive and send official numbers in the next message.

- Dev
Principal Infra SWE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex@brightdata.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightdata.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Performance MAP: long-context benchmarking & TTFT results

Alex — attaching preliminary results and a one-page summary. Key takeaways up front: 

1) Short/median prompts (<=8k): Hosted API meets your latency SLOs easily — TTFT median 30-45ms; throughput scales to ~2k tok/s per A100 instance at concurrency 8.

2) 64k context: expect ~2.5-3x increase in per-token compute cost vs 8k. TTFT median observed ~95-130ms (A100); H100 brings ~20% improvement on TTFT and sustained throughput.

3) 256k context: practical on H100 with quantized model variants; TTFT median ~350-420ms, sustained throughput ~350-500 tok/s at concurrency 8 with warm KV. Cold KV increases TTFT by ~25-35% and reduces throughput further.

4) 512k context: feasible with heavy quantization and memory tuning; concurrency should be limited. We recommend dedicated capacity for production for predictable tail behavior. In these runs, concurrency=1–4 is reasonable; >8 leads to significant queuing and degraded end-to-end TTFT.

5) KV cache behavior: warm cache yields consistent TTFT improvements (median ~15–25%) and better throughput for long sequences because we avoid re-computing prefix attention. Cache effectiveness depends on prompt-repeat ratio: at BrightData's sampled distribution (prefix-heavy), cache is highly beneficial.

6) Cost guidance: we included per-token CPU/GPU seconds and an estimate of per-request cost under your MAP pricing band — see CSV.

Attachments: MAP_Perf_Results_20260301.csv, latency_plots_64k-512k.pdf (full plots).

Next steps proposed in MAP:
- Procurement: lock commitment for Dedicated H100 pool if BrightData expects >20% of requests >64k context.
- Rollout: start with hosted for 8k/64k with autoscale + MAT (Model autoswitching) to quantized variant for >256k windows.
- Eval hooks: add sampling-based quality checks for quantized models to ensure output parity.

If this looks good, Marissa will update the MAP milestones (procurement sign-off by 2026-03-10, Dedicated spin-up by 2026-03-24).

Thanks,
Marissa
